commits.subject: Add configurable revision_map_class option to ScriptDirectory

linked_issues.title: Allow custom RevisionMap subclass for pluggable revision ordering

source.description:
Closes #1804

## Summary

- Adds a `revision_map_class` configuration option to `ScriptDirectory`, allowing a custom `RevisionMap` subclass to be specified via `alembic.ini` or `pyproject.toml` using a dotted Python path (e.g. `mypackage.custom:CustomRevisionMap`)
- Adds a `resolve_dotted_name()` utility for resolving `"module:ClassName"` strings to Python objects, with clear error messages for import/attribute failures
- Exports `RevisionMap` from the `alembic.script` package for convenient subclassing

## Motivation

See #1804 for full context. In short: there is currently no way to customize how Alembic orders concurrent, unrelated migrations (multiple heads) without monkey-patching. This small change (one new keyword argument with a `None` default, entirely opt-in) opens up an extension point for external packages to implement custom ordering — such as git-history-based ordering — by subclassing `RevisionMap` and overriding `_topological_sort()`.

## Changes

- **`alembic/util/pyfiles.py`**: New `resolve_dotted_name()` utility
- **`alembic/script/base.py`**: New `revision_map_class` parameter on `ScriptDirectory.__init__()` and `from_config()`, with subclass validation
- **`alembic/script/__init__.py`**: Export `RevisionMap` for convenient subclassing
- **Templates**: Commented-out `revision_map_class` option in all ini/toml templates
- **Tests**: 12 new tests for the utility function, config integration, and validation
- **Changelog**: `docs/build/unreleased/revision_map_class.rst`

## Test plan

- [x] `resolve_dotted_name()` tests (colon format, dot format, error cases)
- [x] `revision_map_class` via constructor and via `from_config()`
- [x] Validation rejects non-subclasses, unresolvable modules/attributes
- [x] `RevisionMap` properly exported from `alembic.script`
- [x] Full `test_config.py` suite passes (75 tests)

story.headline: `ScriptDirectory` will build a `RevisionMap` subclass named in config instead of the built-in one.

beats.label: Need

beats.label: Next
beats.text: Nothing subclasses it here. The ordering itself is unchanged; only who decides it can move.

intent_delta.stated: This small change (one new keyword argument with a `None` default, entirely opt-in) opens up an extension point for external packages.

also_does.summary: Adds `resolve_dotted_name`, a general utility exported from `alembic.util`, not scoped to this option.
It accepts `module.Class` as well as the `module:Class` form the templates and changelog document.

contracts.name: revision_map_class
contracts.after: dotted path to a RevisionMap subclass (default alembic.script.revision.RevisionMap)

behavior.summary: With the option unset the built object is what it was. With it set, `from_config` resolves the dotted name, refuses a class that is not a `RevisionMap`, and passes it on.

deltas.summary: `from_config` gains a resolve-and-check step before it builds anything.
`__init__` picks the class instead of naming it.
A misconfigured name now fails the command rather than the migration.

steps.title: The resolver
steps.why: Everything else depends on what this accepts and what it raises. It is the only genuinely new code.

annotations.text: The second form is `rpartition`, so `a.b.C` splits at the last dot. The templates and the changelog document only the colon form.
`import_module` runs the target module at this point, which is inside every alembic command, not inside a migration.

steps.title: The keyword argument
steps.why: The constructor is the direct entry point, and it is where the default is decided.

annotations.text: The one removed line in the change was here: `self.revision_map = revision.RevisionMap(self._load_revisions)`.
Whatever arrived is called. This path performs no subclass check of its own.

steps.title: Reading and checking the option
steps.why: The config path is the one users reach, and the only one that validates.

annotations.text: `get_alembic_option` reads the ini section first and `[tool.alembic]` in pyproject.toml second, so an ini value wins.
`CommandError` is what alembic prints as a message rather than a traceback, so this surfaces as a command failure.
The keyword is passed last, alongside the other options `from_config` collects.

steps.title: The two exports
steps.why: One line each in two `__init__` files, both load-bearing: `util.resolve_dotted_name` in step 3, and `RevisionMap` for subclassing.

steps.title: What the tests pin
steps.why: Half the changed lines. They state the accepted formats, both failure messages, and that the default is untouched.

annotations.text: `type(script.revision_map) is RevisionMap` rather than isinstance, so a subclass would fail this.
The constructor path is tested with a subclass, and the config path with a rejection. Neither test sets a subclass through config.

checks.title: Only the config path checks the subclass
checks.why: `from_config` raises `CommandError` at base.py:204 for a class that is not a `RevisionMap`. `ScriptDirectory(...)` called directly instantiates whatever it is handed.
checks.question: Do you build `ScriptDirectory` directly anywhere, where that check does not run?

checks.title: A dotted name is imported during every command
checks.why: `resolve_dotted_name` calls `importlib.import_module` inside `from_config`, which runs for all fifteen commands in `alembic/command.py`.
checks.question: Is the module holding your subclass importable in every environment that runs an alembic command, including CI and containers?

checks.title: The same key can be set in two files
checks.why: `get_alembic_option` searches the configparser section before the toml one, so a value in `alembic.ini` takes precedence over `[tool.alembic]`.
checks.question: Do any of your environments carry both an `alembic.ini` and a `[tool.alembic]` block?

checks.title: `_topological_sort` decides the order migrations run in
checks.why: It is called from `iterate_revisions` at revision.py:822, which is the walk behind upgrade and downgrade. The description names it as the method a subclass would override.
checks.question: Would a different ordering of concurrent unrelated heads be safe to apply in your deployments?
